subject: Sales: Prompt set collection & model-fit follow-up (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: model fit & prompt collection (Acme)

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the thoughtful discussion. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Model fit thoughts
- Recommended starting points: Redwood-verified 16B (cost-efficient, strong instruction-following) and Redwood-verified 34B (better for multi-turn summarization/complex extraction).
- If the scope grows to longer context or higher fidelity, we can evaluate a 70B variant but we typically reserve that for more complex reasoning workloads.

2) Benchmarks and evals
- I uploaded our internal benchmark/runbook and the initial evaluation harness to the folder below. We'll run a model-fit eval using your sample prompts once you share them.
  https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEvalBench

3) Prompt set collection request (action for Acme)
- Please provide: representative prompts, edge cases, expected outputs (where applicable), and any redaction requirements.
- Attached is a small template you can drop prompts into: prompt_set_template.csv (attached).
- Helpful guidance: mark which prompts contain PII or customer-sensitive fields and flag any business-critical failure modes (e.g., hallucination around product specs).

4) Timeline & next steps
- If you can share an initial set by EOD next Thursday (2026-08-20), we’ll run an initial eval and get back with model recommendations, latency/cost estimates, and a short benchmark report.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk through redaction guidance and sample outputs.

Open question for you: do you have a preferred approach for PII handling (client-side redaction vs. allowlist masking)? If you send a quick note we’ll adapt our eval to match.

Thanks — looking forward to the prompts.
—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

Attachment: prompt_set_template.csv

From: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@acme.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T14:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & prompt collection (Acme)

Thanks Marissa — great call. Attaching an initial dump of common prompts from our support and docs teams (acme_prompts.csv). A few quick notes: 
- Many prompts include email addresses and order IDs; should we pre-mask those or leave them as-is for the eval?
- We have a handful of legal/regulatory edge cases that sometimes trip up models (contract clause summaries).
- Budget for this phase is limited, so if the 70B class is significantly more expensive we probably won’t proceed there initially.

We’ll aim to get a fuller set to you by next Thursday. Thanks again.

—
Jordan Meyers
Product Operations Lead | Acme Corp
jordan.meyers@acme.com

Attachment: acme_prompts.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & prompt collection (Acme)

Appreciate the quick send, Jordan — got the CSV. Short answers and plan: 

On PII/redaction
- Recommendation: client-side redaction of direct identifiers before sending for evaluation (emails, SSNs, exact account numbers). For fields where context is needed, replace with consistent pseudonyms (e.g., <CUSTOMER_1>) so the model can still learn patterns without exposing raw identifiers.
- We can also run an eval variant where we keep tokens present to measure model behavior on unredacted text if you want a risk baseline — we’ll only do this with explicit approval.

On models and cost
- Agree that 70B is likely outside budget for initial testing. We’ll prioritize Redwood-verified 16B and 34B families for the first pass and include a cost/latency comparison in the report.

Next steps (what we’ll do)
- Internal: Logan/Ben will run the prompt set through our eval harness and return a short benchmark PDF highlighting quality regressions, latency, and cost. Expect initial results within 3 business days of receiving the fuller prompt set.
- I’ll attach a short internal benchmark once we’ve completed the first run (see model_benchmark_report.pdf placeholder).

Action for Acme
- Please: (1) mark PII in the template or replace with pseudonyms, (2) call out any must-pass prompts, and (3) share any redaction policy language you want us to follow so our eval mirrors production constraints.

Thanks — we’ll get started as soon as we have the fuller set.

—
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: model_benchmark_report.pdf (placeholder)

Fwd’ing Acme’s initial prompts and the redaction question — please run the initial eval when you have a moment and flag any quality regressions or hallucination patterns, especially on the contract-summary prompts. Key asks: 
- Run 16B and 34B candidate models, compare ROUGE/BLEU where applicable and a handful of human-eval checks for hallucination.
- Produce a short doc listing: top 5 failure modes, latency at 8k context, estimated per-1M token cost for each candidate.
- If you see data leakage or outputs that could reveal PII in unredacted mode, call it out explicitly.

I’ll coordinate with Jordan once we have the initial PDF so they can decide next steps. Thanks.
